pr.title: Add a rewrite skill that revises existing text and writes it back
pr.head: 6cda373eb9c603fcca480b62c9280e289478338a

summary: Projector's skills write prose by one writing guide, skills/writing.md. The write skill applies that guide to any prose a user asks for. Revising text that already exists takes two more steps: finding the text, and putting the result back. A file is easy, but a pull request description, a review comment, or a commit message each needs its own command to read it and another to update it.

This pull request adds a rewrite skill for that. It takes pasted text or a reference to text, reads it with the command that fits the reference, revises it with write's steps, and writes it back where it lives. It writes back only when the user wrote the text and something can edit it; otherwise it returns the revised text in the reply. write's description narrows to new prose, so the two skills don't compete for one request.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Skill: a SKILL.md file of instructions an agent follows, published from the root skills/ directory to both Claude Code and Codex.
  • Write back: replace the original text in place, such as with gh pr edit --body-file.
  • Author check: compare who wrote the text with the user running the skill before writing back.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first review, of 01f8079, opened two threads: a line in docs/plugins.md that broke the paragraph's wrapping, and write's Codex interface, which still offered it for revisions. It also suggested naming user.login for gh api reads.
  • Three commits fixed both threads and took the suggestion, and the review of 6cda373 found the head clean.
  • One question stays open: should rewrite keep Projector's hidden <!-- projector-… --> marker comments when it rewrites a pull request description or a review?

groups.title: The rewrite skill
groups.kicker: How rewrite finds text, revises it, and decides whether to write it back
intro: The skill has three parts. Find the text maps each kind of reference to a read command and a write-back command. Rewrite it reuses write's steps and adds rules only an existing text needs, such as keeping every fact and identifier and updating links when a heading changes. Hand it over writes the result back, or returns it in the reply when the source can't be edited, someone else wrote it, the commit is pushed, or the user asks for the text.
The author check is what keeps the skill within Projector's rule that seeing a text doesn't authorize changing it.

files.note: The new skill: the reference table, the rules for an existing text, and when to write back.

checks.text: "Keep the format the text must have" doesn't name HTML marker comments, such as the projector-summary block at the end of a pull request description. The review asks whether it should.
The author check names author.login for gh pr view and gh issue view, and user.login for a comment or review read through gh api, the field each command returns.

files.note: Codex's display name, short description, and default prompt for the new skill.

groups.title: Narrowing write to new prose
groups.kicker: write's description and Codex interface stop claiming revisions
intro: write's frontmatter description now covers only new prose and points revisions to rewrite, and its Codex interface says the same. The host reads these to pick a skill, so the change decides which skill a request to revise text reaches.

files.note: Codex's short description and default prompt for write now describe writing new prose, not revising.

groups.title: Documentation and packaging
groups.kicker: Naming the new skill where the skills are listed, and in the packaging test
intro: The README, docs/plugins.md, and the writing guide's opening name rewrite. The packaging test's set of published skills gains rewrite, so the test fails if the skill directory goes missing or another appears.

checks.text: The repository's full gate passed at 6cda373: 1097 unit tests with one skip, project check, both claude plugin validate commands, 144 hooks tests, hooks/typecheck.sh, and git diff --check.
